rule_title: ONE coherent thematic improvement per round
message: The commit bundles several arguably distinct themes in a single round: (a) regulator attestation packs (stepback/attestation.py, +426 LOC), (b) ambient process-global autorecord (stepback/autorecord.py, +224 LOC), (c) cross-trace diff (stepback/trace_diff.py, +501 LOC), (d) RFC 6902 JSON Patch primitive (stepback/jsonpatch.py, +214 LOC), and (e) substitutions/CLI extensions (+257/+321 LOC). While these can be framed as 'expanding the record/replay/substitute surface area', a stricter reading of Rule 2 would expect one theme (e.g. attestation OR cross-trace diff). Recommend the next round either justify the unifying theme in dossier or split future work.
evidence: stepback/autorecord.py: 'Process-global ambient recorder for `stepback record -- python script.py`.'
stepback/trace_diff.py: 'Cross-trace diff: structural comparison of two recorded `.sb` traces.'
stepback/jsonpatch.py: 'RFC 6902 JSON Patch (subset) + RFC 6901 JSON Pointer.'
git diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat shows 4584 insertions across 5 new top-level modules

message: 32 .pyc files under stepback/__pycache__/ and tests/__pycache__/ are included in the commit. These are regenerated on every test run and should be gitignored. Not a constitution rule per se, but pollutes the diff and makes review harder.

tests/fixtures/ contains only agent.py / parallel_agent.py helper scripts — there is no real recorded `.sb` corpus fixture committed alongside this round. The new tests (test_attestation.py, test_trace_diff.py, test_e2e_substitutions_new.py) appear to synthesize traces in-process rather than load a checked-in real `.sb` artifact. Per Rule 3a, at least one e2e test per round should exercise the pipeline against a real on-disk fixture.
+4584 / -839 LOC across 5 new modules and 7 new test files clearly satisfies Rule 1's preference for ambitious surface expansion. Listed for completeness, not as a violation.
evidence: stepback/attestation.py (426 LOC), stepback/trace_diff.py (501 LOC), stepback/cli.py (+321 LOC)
